name: Glass-Ceramic Seal with Nanoscale Dispersed ZrO₂ Particles
mechanism: Nanoscale ZrO₂ particles in glass-ceramic seal reduce thermal expansion mismatch via constrained sintering.
failure_link: Mitigates microcrack initiation in seal by lowering differential expansion (thermal-cycling-fatigue).
source: credit-register lead (1.0.0; owner-cited win, restored per Amendment 2 P0-1)
repair_directives: Run the rule-of-mixtures CTE SIGN CHECK on the ZrO2 dispersion (ZrO2 CTE ~10-11 ppm/K may RAISE the composite CTE) — anchor the mechanism on constrained sintering densification, not CTE reduction alone (Amendment 1 salvage)
Fix the malformed DOI 10.1002/advs.77388 or cite the packet records only (Amendment 1 salvage)
The falsification test MUST carry the constraint's own criteria: 500 thermal cycles 25->800 C at 5 C/min, OCV >1.0 V, seal leakage <1% of fuel flow, stack mass +<=2% (Amendment 1 salvage)
The seal is a GLASS-CERAMIC IONIC INSULATOR — never an electronic conductor (the R2 LSM substitution is the audited defect)
